deities: No single presiding deity - the seven-level walls carry shrine niches depicting Vishnu's Dashavataras, plus Brahma, Shiva, Lakshmi, apsaras and sadhus; water itself is treated as the sanctum

history.dynasty: Solanki (Chaulukya) - commissioned by Queen Udayamati in memory of her husband King Bhima I
history.summary: 11th-century stepwell at Patan, ~64 m long, 20 m wide and 27 m deep, descending seven levels. Built c. 1063 CE by Queen Udayamati in memory of her husband King Bhima I of the Solanki dynasty, in the Maru-Gurjara style. Its walls hold 500+ principal and 1,000+ minor sculptures, with the Dashavataras (ten incarnations of Vishnu, including Buddha) as the central theme - each deity set in its own shrine-like niche, which is why the structure is described as an 'inverted temple' with water at the sanctuary. From around the 13th century the nearby Saraswati river buried it in silt; it stayed hidden for ~700 years until the Archaeological Survey of India excavated it in the late 1980s (work completed 1986). Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014 (India's 31st) and featured on the INR 100 note since 2018. NATURE FLAG: this is a stepwell complex with shrine niches, NOT a conventional temple - there is no regular worship. CSV STATE FLAG: the CSV 'state' column holds the town name - this monument is in GUJARAT (Patan district).

name: Rani ki Vav Temple Shrine
town_description: Patan is a historic city in north Gujarat, the former capital of the Solanki dynasty (then Anhilwara). It is the site of the Rani ki Vav World Heritage stepwell and is also famous for its Patola silk weaving and other Solanki-era monuments.
tradition: Hinduism (sacred architecture - a stepwell with Vaishnavite shrine imagery, not a worship temple)
